children.subject: PUT /api/products/prices changes only the price lists in the payload and upserts rows by id
children.question: does PUT /api/products/prices replace a product's prices in other price lists
children.body: Sending PUT /api/products/prices with rows for a single price list changed only that list. The same products' rows in two other price lists came back identical (ids, list, sale, minQuantity). A row sent with its existing id was updated in place and kept that id; rows sent without an id were added. The source shows the flip side: an existing row in a list that is in the payload but is left out of it is deleted, so a product's full desired set for that list must be sent.

children.subject: storefront barcode search leaves barcode:"x" a literal filter with no fields configured, and scannerEnabled=false hides only the scan button
children.question: How does the storefront behave on /search?barcode= and in the header search bars under each barcode-search store setting?
children.body: Observed on a vc-frontend build carrying the barcode scanner search setup (theme PR 2501, x-catalog PR 113, catalog PR 909). Store settings are read at app load, so a change is seen only after a full reload. Defaults (scannerEnabled true, fields empty): the Barcode scan button shows in the desktop search bar and in the mobile (390 px) overlay bar; typing a GTIN into the box is a full-text search (?q=) that also matches the value inside other products' names; /search?barcode=<value> is still routed to the barcode heading, but the products query carries barcode:"<value>" as a literal filter term and returns 0, so the page shows 'No products found for barcode <value>'. scannerEnabled false with fields configured: the Barcode scan button disappears from both bars, yet /search?barcode=<value> still expands to the configured fields and opens the product, so the switch hides the entry point only. A whitespace-only ?barcode=%20%20 is not trimmed: it renders the empty state with a blank value in the heading, no error. On a category route (for example /<category-slug>?barcode=<value>) the term is applied inside that category's scope and the plain category heading is used.

why: (b) a later contradicting note disputes only the count clause of the configurations search and confirms every other part

children.subject: a product's configurability is a separate entity keyed by productId, not a field on the product record
children.question: how do I tell from product data whether a product is configurable
children.body: A product's configurability is NOT a field on the product. GET /api/catalog/products/{id} returns the full CatalogProduct record -- 60+ fields including mainProductId, variations and productType -- and carries no isConfigurable and no configuration at all, so reading products can never tell you. The configuration is a separate entity keyed by productId. Note also that productType is Physical/Digital/null -- 'Configurable' is not one of its values, so filtering products by type finds nothing either. The storefront GraphQL Product type does expose a computed isConfigurable, but only for products the search index holds, so it answers a narrower question than the REST route does. A catalog can hold the configuration OPTION products (the parts a configuration is assembled from) and categories named for configurables while having no configurable product at all -- the options are ordinary products and look like any other.

children.subject: the configurations search with an empty criteria body counts inactive configurations too
children.question: how do I count the configurable products on a deployment
children.body: POST /api/catalog/products/configurations/search is where configurability is read, but an empty criteria body counts configurations regardless of isActive, so its totalCount is not the number of configurable products on the deployment. After creating one configuration and then deactivating it, the empty body returns totalCount 1 while {isActive:true} returns 0 and the product reads isConfigurable false. Since there is no delete route, deactivated rows are permanent, so the empty-body count drifts upward from the number of genuinely configurable products and never comes back. Use {isActive:true} for the count.

children.subject: the Lists page disables Create list once the user owns the per-user list limit
children.question: Why is Create list disabled on /account/lists?
children.body: On /account/lists the Create list button disables once the signed-in user owns as many lists as the store's per-user lists limit allows - an account already at the limit sees a permanently disabled button, BY DESIGN.

children.subject: a list's share link lives only in the list Settings dialog, editable from the card and view-only from the detail page
children.question: Where is a list's share link on /account/lists?
children.body: The list Settings dialog is one shared component: opened from the list card's menu it is editable, opened from the button on the list detail page it is view-only with its fields disabled. There is no Share button on the list card or detail page; the share URL with its copy icon lives only inside the Settings dialog, shown when the list's sharing scope supports a link and the user is a corporate member.
